sources.entry: markdown - A Python implementation of John Gruber's Markdown.

summary.one_liner: Python-Markdown is a Python implementation of John Gruber's Markdown text-to-HTML syntax, extensible through a set of available extensions.
summary.what_it_does: The library converts Markdown text into HTML via markdown.markdown(), and is installable with pip install markdown. The README says it is almost completely compliant with the reference Markdown implementation, with a few known issues listed in its Features documentation. Additional syntax is provided by extensions listed under Available Extensions. Fuller installation and usage docs are in the docs/ directory of the distribution, and the project site hosts the change log. Bugs and questions go to the project's bug tracker.
use_cases: convert markdown text to html in python
render markdown documents in a python web app
add extra markdown syntax with extensions
process markdown files in a python build pipeline
notable: Near-complete compliance with John Gruber's reference Markdown implementation
Extension system providing additional Markdown features
caveats: README notes a few known issues with reference compliance; see Features docs for details
Advanced installation and usage details live in the docs/ directory rather than the README
